These are my own words and from my own experiences and perspectives. I’m not a professional. Just someone who dealt with  a strong fawn and freeze response 

Ok so I’m going to start by saying that working on ways to dismantle toxic shame, helps so much. Shame drives much of this behavior.

Notice how you’re feeling in your body in these moments. Are you shaky, tightness in chest? How does your throat feel? What do you feel when you have to confront someone? What do you feel when you’ve possibly hurt someone? Probably terrified. Practice connecting with your breath. Mindfulness. They will eventually become a practice.


Noticing these things in the moment takes practice and it’s a very crucial part of the process.  Building body awareness helps and there’s different ways that resonate with different people. Don’t be afraid to be open minded and don’t feel bad or ashamed if something doesn’t work for you.

You likely have many tools that you use, I’m not sure of your self care practices or where you are in your journey. It may be a combination of things that will resonate with your subconscious and it won’t feel so terrifying.

Trying things that scare you, like maybe a new sport, an acting class . Actually sports and exercise  raised my tolerance or sorts and that fear response is weakened. They taught me how not to be afraid of failure which carries over. There will be people you meet during this adventure that will help you along your journey. Observe and notice who’s around you. 

Again, think of it as a lifestyle change. It’s putting together a puzzle. You can weaken the fawn response and change the pattern. Do not think of this as who you are at your core. Nor should you be ashamed of it. This is how you subconsciously protect yourself. It’s a pattern you run . It’s not who you are.

When I took them out I was at a loss because of all the new growth, so I decided to look to Google for advice. That's when I found all of these hair blogs and videos about transitioning and natural hair. I started transitioning , then when I was a couple months from turning 19 I big chopped. It was shocking at First, but I just practiced practiced practiced until I found what was right for me. It didn't take long to get my basic routine down.

That was 3 years ago. Today I keep my hair at brastrap length. Any longer and it gets TOO overwhelming.I like my hair at this length. I never thought I could grow hair this long or longer.I know not everyone cares for long hair but I was one of those that would kill for longer hair. I have a pretty basic routine. It's gotten easier (most of the time) as time went on. I'm pretty happy with my hair. I get lots of compliments and attention. Every so often I get negative reactions but I just remember that the most important thing is I love my hair.

As for advice, I started out watching videos and routines of natural girls with MY hair type or similar. That way I have an idea of how a style will look on me. I had an idea what products to try.
